concept.name: Buying climax
concept.definition: In Wyckoff's distribution schematic, the buying climax (BC) is the terminal event of an advance: a marked expansion of volume and price spread as urgent public buying near the top is filled by professional interests distributing positions. It is a descriptive label for auction behavior, confirmed only when further upside progress fails.
concept.intuition: The most euphoric buying tends to appear exactly where large operators need that public demand to sell into without depressing the price themselves.
concept.mechanics: Identified as a wide-spread up bar or cluster on the heaviest volume of the advance following an extended uptrend, often coinciding with good news; the BC high sets the upper boundary of the ensuing trading range, followed by an automatic reaction and secondary tests.
concept.failure_modes: Strong trends produce repeated climax-like bars that resolve into continuation rather than distribution, so treating every high-volume up-spike as a buying climax leads to premature shorts.
concept.misconceptions: A buying climax does not require a collapse to follow; it marks where supply met demand, and the market can also resolve sideways or even grind higher once that supply is absorbed.
concept.example: A stock rallies 40% in two months, then gaps up on earnings with its widest range and highest volume of the year, closing mid-range; the next two weeks fail to exceed that high, and the spike is labeled the buying climax.

citations.source: LuxAlgo — Wyckoff Accumulation Schematic (distribution mirror with a buying climax instead of a selling climax)
